## Process lifecycle

- Run long-lived servers and watchers in a persistent session such as tmux.
- Do not background them in bounded commands without explicit detachment and cleanup.
- After a timeout, inspect the process and endpoint before retrying or claiming failure.

## Linux browser and WebGPU capture

- Use the preinstalled `playwright-cli` executable from Actions or SSH.
- Use its headed Chromium, persistent Xvfb display, and SwiftShader configuration.
- Run `playwright-cli open http://localhost:3002` for the Pascal development server.
- Load a saved scene. Wait for actual geometry and the active WebGPU renderer.
- Run `playwright-cli screenshot --filename=screenshots/linux.png` after creating the output directory.
- Inspect the image. Reject loading screens, empty grids, and blank canvases.
- Report SwiftShader as CPU software rendering. Do not claim GPU hardware acceleration.
- Inspect `$HOME/.local/share/omgithub-playwright/linux.json` for launch settings.
- Use `playwright-cli --help` for commands and named sessions. Pass configuration only to `open`.

## Mobile browser games

- Support Android and iOS phones and tablets with responsive layouts and usable touch controls.
- Keep gameplay and controls visible within safe areas and avoid browser gesture conflicts.
- Add tilt controls only when appropriate; offer touch alternatives and request iOS motion permission from a user gesture when needed.
- Follow explicit device and control requirements in the user request.

Scope summary:
- After entering store (both routes) gameplay inside store:
  - Find 10 scattered canned foods.
  - Find fuel room locked with password door (keypad). Note says password is "last two digits years, days, months". Bloody text on other wall: "Build in 12/12/1926" → password 261212. Interpret: "last two digits years, days, months" = 26 (year), 12 (day), 12 (month) → 261212.
  - Input keypad UI (6 digits) or choices? Need interact with keypad, enter 261212.
  - Pick up fuel can; when about to exit, shotgun guy shows up at door, says "Stop", "Give me the truck key". Choices: Threatened him / Give the keys. Both lead to same scene but threatened still holding gun. He locks? Wording: "then you lock at the locker beside the doors and run and quickly drop and block the door and he try to get in shouting -cutscene end-." Probably "then you look at the locker beside the doors and run and quickly drop and block the door". He tries to get in, shouting. Cutscene end → 20 sec timer.
  - 20-second sequence: guy shouting at door trying to get in. If timer about to run out he says "Wait I'm about to open". Scissors Jack on table, use quickly to open jammed iron doors; QTE rotate button quickly to lift doors; door lift slightly, crawl in, kick jack, guy says "Noooo!".
  - Then while standing up another guy with dagger appears, pins you to wall, swipe right to kick him; chase starts, he says "That's it!".
  - Run to truck. While crawling to gate hole he grabs your leg: choice shoot him or run. If shoot, first guy says "Jaaake!" and runs to body, but you run. If run, swipe right to kick him then run.
  - Get in truck, try to start engine (swipe down QTE), engine fails, try again starts, they shoot windows, drive away, tire shot and boom accident; Chapter 1 finish.
  - Cinematic death animation, evening vibes, camera movement polish.

That's a large action sequence with many QTEs and cutscenes. We need implement within reasonable code. We can reuse existing environment and build interior.

Plan implementation:
1. Add store interior as gameplay environment (actual interior) with 10 cans, fuel room, lockers, tables, etc. Currently gameplay scene is compound with a basic store interior behind doors. We can build the interior as a separate detailed room and transition player inside after entering. Or extend compound interior with collectible cans and fuel room. Simpler: when entering store (shoot or vent), load an interior Scene/Game phase with walkable room. Since world compound already has interior but with furniture; we can add props and colliders. But gameplay camera and player could walk inside if we remove building collision and doors. The compound interior is 42x22 with store furniture; but lacks detailed fuel room. We can extend buildFurnitureCompound interior with:
   - Fuel room in back-left with iron door and keypad.

Instead new gameplay phase: after enter door, switch to interior mode and objective collect cans. For "other way" vent, after vent transition player inside.

Maybe easier to create a new `InteriorGame` class/scene for the inside store. This decouples from compound and lets us design precisely. Flow:

## Objective
- Build a complete, playable 3D monster-apocalypse story game in Three.js, with a cinematic opening and interactive furniture-store gameplay.
- Expand the story through scavenging, a fuel-room standoff, a timed escape, a chase, and a Chapter 1 ending.

## Requirements
- Main menu: forest road, “WATCH OUT!” sign, wooden Play button.
- Opening story: Tim’s abandoned-city journey, skeleton encounter, highway, crashed airplane near a school, fogged-car skeleton, and arrival at a furniture store.
- Gameplay: boarded “TRESPASSER WILL BE SHOT” gate and crouch-through hole; yellow-walled furniture store, glass doors, trash, and a choice to shoot the doors or find another way in.
- Alternate route: go around the building, climb boxes, enter through a vent, then show “you follow as your character story” story information.
- Store interior: collect 10 scattered food cans, find fuel behind password-locked doors, solve `261212` from the note “last two digits years,days, months” and bloody “Build in 12/12/1926.”
- Fuel-room encounter: masked first man with shotgun demands the truck key; choice to threaten him or give him the key. Both lead into the same escape scene, with Tim holding the gun if he threatened the man.
- Escape sequence: Tim notices a locker, runs, drops and blocks the iron door; the man shouts and has a 20-second timer. A scissor jack at a table and a rapid button-rotation QTE lift the door enough to crawl under; Tim kicks the jack away.
- Chase: a second tattooed man with a dagger pins Tim to a wall; swipe right to kick him, then run to the truck. At the gate hole, choose to shoot or run; include the corresponding “Jaaake!” reaction or kick-and-run.
- Truck escape: swipe down to start the engine; first attempt fails, second succeeds; attackers shoot the windows, a tire is shot, and the crash ends Chapter 1.
- Make the story cinematic, polished, evening-toned, and include expressive, human characters and improved dialogue/talking animations. Tim is a teenage boy wearing an old T-shirt; the first man wears a mask; the second man has tattoos. Do not ask clarifying questions.

## Decisions
- Use Three.js with a locally vendored module, custom HTML/CSS interface, and locally bundled fonts.
- Use procedurally generated 3D assets, textures, and audio; no external game assets are required so far.
- Keep both store-door choices continuing the story; the alternate route uses the vent and story-information card.

## Work State
### Completed
- Built the UI shell for menu, cutscenes, gameplay HUD, choices, story information, pause/options, and ending.
- Added local Three.js and fonts.
- Added substantial procedural texture, model, world, audio, cutscene, and gameplay code.
- Added human-character models via `createBandit()` and began expanding character detail; latest user request for improved character appearance, expressions, and dialogue animation remains to implement.

### Active
- Complete `src/main.js` and connect the existing UI, renderer, game, cutscenes, and input.
- Implement the 10-can/fuel/password sequence, masked-man choices, timed door escape and QTE, tattooed-man chase, gate choices, truck-start gestures, crash, and Chapter 1 ending.
- Refine Tim and both men to match the user’s character descriptions; add facial expressions and talking animations.
- Test the full game in a browser and fix issues, including desktop/mobile layouts.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Inspect the current UI IDs and existing modules; implement the missing application entry point in `src/main.js`.
2. Continue the gameplay flow after entering the furniture store, including scavenging, password puzzle, standoff, QTE, chase, and crash ending.
3. Improve character models, expressions, animation, and dialogue delivery.
4. Run the project and test the complete story and responsive controls; fix discovered issues.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: UI structure and element IDs, including story-information card.
- `styles.css`: Visual design, responsive layout, captions, chapter card, and story card.
- `src/game.js`: Interactive furniture-compound gameplay and current door-choice branches.
- `src/cutscenes.js`: Cinematic scene director and opening sequence.
- `src/world.js`: Procedural environments, furniture compound, and store interiors.
- `src/models.js`: Character and environment models, including `TimCharacter` and `createBandit()`.
- `src/textures.js`: Procedural textures and signs.
- `src/audio.js`: Synthesized music, ambience, and sound effects.
- `start.sh`: Project start script.
- `vendor/three.module.js`: Local Three.js module.
- `fonts/`: Locally bundled interface fonts.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted.
- The latest recorded work added `createBandit()` variants, but did not yet update Tim to the requested old T-shirt look or implement expressions/talking animation.
- No browser testing or full application run is recorded.
- The user’s newest gameplay requirements extend beyond the existing implementation; treat them as pending work.

import { startForCapture } from './capture-start.mjs'
import captures from './wip-screenshots.cjs'
import { createRequire } from 'node:module'
import { readFileSync, mkdirSync } from 'node:fs'
import { join } from 'node:path'
const runtime = join(process.env.HOME, '.local/share/omgithub-playwright')
const require = createRequire(join(runtime, 'package.json'))
const { chromium } = require('playwright')
captures.instrument({ chromium })
const config = JSON.parse(readFileSync(join(runtime, process.platform === 'darwin' ? 'metal.json' : 'linux.json'), 'utf8'))
if (process.platform === 'linux') process.env.DISPLAY ||= ':' + readFileSync(join(runtime, 'display'), 'utf8').trim()
const url = process.env.CAPTURE_URL, output = process.env.CAPTURE_DIR
if (!url || !output) throw new Error('Set CAPTURE_URL and CAPTURE_DIR.')
mkdirSync(output, { recursive: true })
const transient = error => { throw Object.assign(error, { exitCode: 75 }) }
let browser
try {
  browser = await chromium.launch({ ...config.browser.launchOptions, timeout: 30000 }).catch(transient)
  for (const [name, width, height] of [['desktop', 1440, 900], ['mobile', 390, 844]]) {
    const page = await browser.newPage({ viewport: { width, height } }).catch(transient)
    page.setDefaultTimeout(30000)
    const failures = []
    page.on('pageerror', error => { console.error(error.message); failures.push(error.message) })
    page.on('response', response => { if (response.status() >= 400 && new URL(response.url()).origin === new URL(url).origin) failures.push(`HTTP ${response.status()}: ${response.url()}`) })
    const response = await page.goto(url, { waitUntil: 'load', timeout: 45000 }).catch(transient)
    if (!response?.ok()) throw Object.assign(new Error(`HTTP ${response?.status()} loading preview`), { exitCode: !response || [408, 429, 500, 502, 503, 504].includes(response.status()) ? 75 : 1 })
    await page.locator(process.env.CAPTURE_READY_SELECTOR || 'body').waitFor({ state: 'visible' })
    await page.waitForFunction(() => document.fonts.status === 'loaded')
    const start = await startForCapture(page, {
      enabled: process.env.CAPTURE_AUTO_START !== 'false',
      selector: process.env.CAPTURE_START_SELECTOR || ''
    })
    console.log(`Capture ${name}: auto-start ${start.clicked ? 'clicked' : start.reason}`)
    await page.waitForTimeout(1000)
    await page.screenshot({ path: join(output, `final-${name}.png`), timeout: 30000 }).catch(error => {
      if (error.name === 'TimeoutError' || !browser.isConnected()) transient(error)
      throw error
    })
    if (process.env.CAPTURE_STRICT === '1' && failures.length) throw new Error(`Published build failed: ${failures.join('; ')}`)
    await page.close()
  }
} catch (error) { console.error(error); process.exitCode = error.exitCode || 1 }
finally { await browser?.close().catch(error => { console.error(error); process.exitCode ||= 75 }) }

## Objective
- Build a complete, playable 3D monster-apocalypse story game in Three.js, with a cinematic opening and interactive furniture-store gameplay.
- Expand the story through scavenging, a fuel-room standoff, a timed escape, a chase, and a Chapter 1 ending.

## Requirements
- Main menu: forest road, “WATCH OUT!” sign, wooden Play button.
- Opening story: Tim’s abandoned-city journey, skeleton encounter, highway, crashed airplane near a school, fogged-car skeleton, and arrival at a furniture store.
- Gameplay: boarded “TRESPASSER WILL BE SHOT” gate and crouch-through hole; yellow-walled furniture store, glass doors, trash, and a choice to shoot the doors or find another way in.
- Alternate route: go around the building, climb boxes, enter through a vent, then show “you follow as your character story” story information.
- Store interior: collect 10 scattered food cans, find fuel behind password-locked doors, solve `261212` from the note “last two digits years,days, months” and bloody “Build in 12/12/1926.”
- Fuel-room encounter: masked first man with shotgun demands the truck key; choice to threaten him or give him the key. Both lead into the same escape scene, with Tim holding the gun if he threatened the man.
- Escape sequence: Tim notices a locker, runs, drops and blocks the iron door; the man shouts and has a 20-second timer. A scissor jack at a table and a rapid button-rotation QTE lift the door enough to crawl under; Tim kicks the jack away.
- Chase: a second tattooed man with a dagger pins Tim to a wall; swipe right to kick him, then run to the truck. At the gate hole, choose to shoot or run; include the corresponding “Jaaake!” reaction or kick-and-run.
- Truck escape: swipe down to start the engine; first attempt fails, second succeeds; attackers shoot the windows, a tire is shot, and the crash ends Chapter 1.
- Make the story cinematic, polished, evening-toned, and include expressive, human characters and improved dialogue/talking animations. Tim is a teenage boy wearing an old T-shirt; the first man wears a mask; the second man has tattoos. Do not ask clarifying questions.

## Decisions
- Use Three.js with a locally vendored module, custom HTML/CSS interface, and locally bundled fonts.
- Use procedurally generated 3D assets, textures, and audio; no external game assets are required so far.
- Keep both store-door choices continuing the story; the alternate route uses the vent and story-information card.

## Work State
### Completed
- Built the UI shell for menu, cutscenes, gameplay HUD, choices, story information, pause/options, and ending.
- Added local Three.js and fonts.
- Added substantial procedural texture, model, world, audio, cutscene, and gameplay code.
- Added `src/characters.js` with detailed Tim and bandit models, facial expressions, blinking, and dialogue animation.
- Added `src/interior.js` with a procedurally built furniture-store interior, 10 can pickups, fuel-room keypad and note props, scissor jack, locker, and related state/animation hooks.
- Added `src/escape.js` with a truck scene, Tim in the cab, windshield damage effects, and Mace for the start scene.
- Added keypad, note, QTE, can-count, escape-timer, and death UI markup and styles.
- Updated `src/cutscenes.js` and `src/world.js` to import the new `TimCharacter`.
